issues.failure_explanation: For x in M one has ABCx = 0, so Cx lies in ker_c(AB), but nothing forces Cx into ker(B)^perp; hence x -> Cx need not map M into L. Example: A = [h h] (n=2), B = [1 0 0; 0 1 0], C = (1,-1,1)^T. Then ABC = 0, M = F, and C·1 = (1,-1,1) has a nonzero component along ker(B) = span(e_3), so it is not in L = span(e_1 - e_2). The inference dim M <= dim L is therefore not justified as written.

failure_location.quote: Consider $\Matrix{x} \mapsto \Matrix{Cx}$ as an injective linear operator $\Linop{C} : \mathbb{M} \to \mathbb{L}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compose x -> Cx with the orthogonal projection onto ker(B)^perp; the composite M -> L is well defined and injective (if PCx = 0 then Cx in ker(B), so x in ker(BC) ∩ ker(BC)^perp = 0), and the rest of the argument goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of part 2 (and, via it, part 3, Sylvester's inequality) of the lemma has a gap; the statements themselves are true.
issues.title: Frobenius inequality proof uses an operator M -> L that is not well defined
issues.why_classification: A one-line local fix restores the argument; all conclusions and their downstream uses survive intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $\Matrix{B}^\pinv \Matrix{B} = \Matrix{I}_{m}$ and $\Matrix{C} \Matrix{C}^\pinv = \Matrix{I}_{n}$, then substitute $\Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$ into Theorem~\ref{theorem:pinv_bochner}.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed identity fails already for H = F: take A = [1;1], B = diag(1,2) (full column rank), C = [1]. Then BAC = [1;2] and (BAC)^† = [1/5, 2/5], while C^†A^†B^† = [1/2,1/2]·diag(1,1/2) = [1/2,1/4]. The substitution argument breaks because (BAC·C^†A^†B^†) = B AA^† B^† is not self-adjoint unless B^*B commutes with AA^†. The two-factor identity actually needed later, (Ĝ X)^† = X^†Ĝ^† with Ĝ of full column rank and X of full row rank, is true, but the paper's proof of Lemma cur_column attributes it to Lemma pinv_full_rank, which does not state it; the only stated source for such a product rule is the false part 2.

failure_location.quote: If $\Matrix{B} \in \F^{k \times m}$ has full column rank and $\Matrix{C} \in \F^{n \times l}$ has full row rank, $(\Matrix{B} \Batrix{A} \Matrix{C})^\pinv = \Matrix{C}^\pinv \Batrix{A}^\pinv \Matrix{B}^\pinv$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace part 2 by a correct statement, e.g. (B A C)^† = C^† A^† B^† for B with orthonormal columns and C with orthonormal rows, and separately (Ĝ X)^† = X^† Ĝ^† when Ĝ has full column rank and X full row rank (verified directly via the four Penrose equations); cite the latter in the proof of Lemma cur_column instead of Lemma pinv_full_rank.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of lem:added-8 is false as stated. The product rule used in the proof of Lemma cur_column (and hence cur_twoside, cross_exact) is a valid special case (B = I, Bochner factor of full column rank), so those results survive once a correct product lemma is supplied.
issues.title: Pseudoinverse product formula (BAC)^† = C^†A^†B^† is false under the stated full-rank hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The stated lemma must be weakened to a recognizably comparable version and a correct supporting statement provided for the CUR lemmas; no global architecture changes and the main results are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In our experiment, we choose $\alpha_{\max} = \beta_{\max} = 2$, $m = n = 100$, and $K = 75$.

issues.failure_explanation: For -u'' - α²u = cos(βx) with Dirichlet data, the sine coefficients satisfy (k² - α²) u_k ∝ ∫_0^π cos(βx) sin(kx) dx = k(1 - (-1)^k cos βπ)/(k² - β²), giving denominators (k² - α²)(k² - β²), not (k² + α²)(k² + β²). Moreover, for α ∈ [0,2] the operator -u'' - α²u is singular at α = 1, 2 (α = 2 is a grid point), so the problem as written has no unique solution map there; the displayed formula instead corresponds to a different (coercive) problem. The paper thus misidentifies which solution map the Bochner matrix in Figure 1 represents.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the problem statement to match the computed coefficients (e.g. -u'' + α²u with a right-hand side producing (k²+β²) denominators) or correct the formula to the true coefficients of eq:ode_bvp and restrict α to avoid resonance.
issues.overall_effect: The description of the first numerical experiment is inconsistent: the approximated Bochner matrix is built from the formula, which is not the solution of eq:ode_bvp; reported errors pertain to an unspecified alternative problem. No theorem depends on it.
issues.title: Stated Fourier solution formula does not solve the displayed boundary-value problem
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the experiment's description suffices; no theoretical result or algorithmic guarantee is affected.
